title: Fairness of Explanations in Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Unifying Framework, Axioms, and Future Direction toward Responsible AI

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring procedural unfairness and disparities in explanation stability (GESD) and counterfactual explanations (EDiff) across racial groups, particularly utilizing datasets in criminal justice (COMPAS) and healthcare resource allocation.
Evaluating feature attribution distortions, proxy leakage, and representation-driven inequities across gender groups in domains like employment screening and income prediction (Adult dataset).

Analyzing algorithmic recourse burden disparities, structural actionability barriers, and temporal explanation obsolescence across different socioeconomic groups in credit scoring and lending algorithms.

Measuring explanation stability disparities across interacting protected attributes (e.g., race and gender) using the Multi-Category Explanation Stability Disparity (MESD) metric, which employs label-aware aggregation, empirical-Bayes shrinkage, and CVaR-weighted tail disparity.
